gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much video data the passenger-facing cabin camera records: DashCamTalk tester EricSan's Vantrue N4 Pro S cabin files were 74,410 KB per minute (about 9.9 Mb/s at 1080p), while DashCamTalk tester rcg530 measured 23.8 Mb/s from the VIOFO T330's 1440p IR cabin camera in 3-channel mode, about 2.4 times as much.
standout_why: I opened the three pages ChatGPT cited. productbible.com (cited in both chats) has only maker specs (resolution, sensors, lens angles, rated -20 to 60 °C, card size) and no bitrate or test figure. dashlore.com (cited) quotes named testers only in words: Aussiecams found plates 'clearly readable', DashCamTalk's rcg530 found the T330 'significantly cooler' than a Vantrue E1 Pro, and Julian23 found night plate capture on the N5S 'nearly impossible' without HDR. It gives no figure and says outright that it reports no bitrate or file size. redlinecargarage.com (cited) says it does no testing and repeats listing copy. None of them gives a per-channel bitrate, a cabin-camera bitrate or a measured field of view. I did not open the uncited results (drivespeclab, dashanddrive, idarb, gearnudge, leadfootautomotive, aikinsselect, accessorytested, gigdriverca, hearsmart, verdictfox, productbible's 3-channel page). This finding is new against the cited pages but has not been checked against those.
decides: It doesn't overturn the N4 Pro S as the best-value pick at $279.99. It does split the pick for drivers who mainly want evidence of passenger disputes. The N4 Pro S cabin camera records about 9.9 Mb/s at 1080p (EricSan), and the N5S cabin cameras run 9.8 Mb/s (TonyM's correction, accepted by EricSan). The VIOFO T330 3CH records 23.8 Mb/s at 1440p from its IR cabin camera in 3-channel mode (rcg530). The A329S 3CH tops out at 27 Mbps on the cabin camera (Chuck McCoy's spec list; 196 MB one-minute files work out to about 26 Mb/s). So the VIOFOs win 'best cabin footage', at $499.99 for the T330 3CH on VIOFO's US store on 2026-11-21. Our Vantrue N4 Pro S honestly wins the full-coverage-for-the-money segment. Bitrate stands in for detail; it is not a measured sharpness test. No one cited here measured face detail at night.
candidates: Vantrue Nexus 4 Pro S (N4 Pro S)

findings.label: Cabin camera bitrate measured from recorded files (EricSan, DashCamTalk)
findings.value: 74,410 KB per minute ≈ 9.9 Mb/s (1920×1080, 30 fps, IMX662)
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan, opening post 2025-07-20)
findings.note: Listed under 'Maximum Resolutions'. The post prints the rate as '0.98 Mb/s', but its own file size gives 74,410 × 8 / 60 ≈ 9,921 kb/s ≈ 9.9 Mb/s, so the printed figure is a misplaced decimal point (EricSan admitted the same slip in his N5S thread). The same method checks out on the front channel: 236,202 KB/min → 31.5 Mb/s against the 31.9 Mb/s he printed. The post doesn't say whether all three channels were recording together.

findings.label: Front and rear bitrate measured from recorded files (EricSan, DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Front 31.9 Mb/s (3840×2160, 30 fps, 236,202 KB/min); rear 14.3 Mb/s (2592×1440 as posted, 30 fps, 107,178 KB/min)
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan, 2025-07-20)
findings.note: The post names the rear sensor as IMX678. Vantrue's spec and DashCamTalk's data sheet both say IMX675, 2560×1440. DashCamTalk's data sheet (https://dashcamtalk.com/dash-cam/vantrue-n4-pro-s/, updated 2026-11-21) gives front 32.0 Mbps and rear 14.0 Mbps and lists no cabin bitrate.

findings.label: Bitrate per channel in 3-channel mode, measured from footage (rcg530, DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Front 41.0 Mbps; rear 23.8 Mbps; IR interior 23.8 Mbps
findings.source_title: VIOFO T340 3CH/4CH - Testing/Review - RCG (DashCamTalk forum, rcg530, thread started 2026-09-15)
findings.note: Firmware v1.0_260910, bitrate set to Maximum, taken from recorded 3CH footage. An earlier 53.2 Mbps front figure came from beta firmware and is superseded. Cabin channel is 2560×1440 with a 210° fisheye (maker spec). 23.8 / 9.9 ≈ 2.4× the N4 Pro S cabin rate.

findings.label: Maximum bitrate per channel and one-minute file sizes (Chuck McCoy, DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Front 66 Mbps / 472 MB; rear 27 Mbps / 196 MB; IR interior fisheye 27 Mbps / 196 MB (3CH)
findings.source_title: A329S 3CH (2025) Test & Review PP (DashCamTalk forum, Chuck McCoy, 2025-06-25)
findings.note: These come from the opening post's spec list, not a separate file measurement. 196 MB × 8 / 60 ≈ 26.1 Mb/s, consistent with 27 Mbps.

findings.label: Measured horizontal field of view of the IR cabin camera (Chuck McCoy, DashCamTalk)
findings.value: 179° with fisheye mode off, 203° with fisheye mode on; 105° in both modes with the IR LEDs on
findings.source_title: A329S 3CH (2025) Test & Review PP, post #2 (Chuck McCoy, 2025-06-25)
findings.note: Measured with a wall and a yardstick (his VIOFO Horizontal FOV Database method). He doesn't explain the 105° LEDs-on figure, and I found no other source for it, so don't build a claim on night-time coverage from it. VIOFO advertises 210°.

findings.label: Cabin camera bitrate, 4 channels recording (DashCamTalk thread)
findings.value: 9.8 Mb/s per cabin camera (front cabin and rear cabin, 1080p); parking files 4.9 Mb/s
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue Nexus 5S (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan, opening post 2025-09-04)
findings.note: EricSan's data-rate table (post #12, 2025-09-09) is an image. In text, TonyM (2025-09-10) said 'cameras B and C should be 9.8Mb/s, and the parking files are 4.9Mb/s', and EricSan replied the same day that he had misplaced a decimal and corrected the table. EricSan: 'each set of 3mins of video consumes a total of just about 1GB from four cameras combined.'

findings.label: Bitrate per channel (DashCamTalk data sheet)
findings.value: Front, interior and rear each 14.8 Mbps (2560×1440, 30 fps, IMX675)
findings.note: This is DashCamTalk's data sheet figure; the page doesn't say it was measured. The N4S cabin camera is 1440p, against 1080p on the N4 Pro S.

findings.label: Notebookcheck review (Stephen Pereyra): named judgements, no numeric measurements
findings.value: Hardwire kit 'did not drain' the test car's battery; recording clear and gap-free day and night; 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi preview slow and prone to freezing; default G-sensor over-sensitive
findings.source_title: Vantrue N4 Pro S Review: Clear coverage with a rear camera that gets up close and personal (Notebookcheck, 2025-11-22, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: No bitrate, temperature, power draw or plate-distance figures in the review. Use only as named qualitative judgement.

findings.label: Price, VIOFO US store
findings.value: $499.99, in stock; HK6-F hardwire kit needed for parking mode, $25.99
findings.source_title: VIOFO T330 3CH 4K+2K+2K HDR Dash Cam with 210° Fisheye Cabin Camera (viofo.com)
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py. The store shows no compare-at price. ChatGPT showed $419.99 at Best Buy; I did not open that listing. Hardwire kit: https://www.viofo.com/products/viofo-type-c-hk6-f-acc-hardwire-kit-for-t330-t340-support-parking-mode
